record.paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove the cylindric-partition-motivated identity involving the product T''(L,M,k,k') = product_{i=1}^n [M+L-k_i+k'_i choose L-k_i]_q for L,M in Z_+ and zero-sum integer vectors k,k'. For p>=n, show that the signed A_{n-1} sum over |k|=0 and sigma in S_n of q^{phi_{p,k,sigma}} T''(L,M, p k - sigma + rho, (p-1)k - sigma + rho) equals the corresponding mu-sum with exponent mu(C^{-1} tensor C)mu/2, the q-binomial factor [M+nL - sum_b C^{-1}_{1,b} mu^{(b)}_1 choose nL]_q, and the factor [mu+eta choose mu]_q, where eta=nL(C^{-1}e_1 tensor e_1) - (C^{-1} tensor C)mu and the mu-sum uses the same integrality restriction as the supernomial hierarchy. The case p=n+1 is known from the cited Gessel-Krattenthaler identity; the open problem is the general conjecture supported by computer checks.

evidence.quote: For p = n + 1 the above is identity

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $n\ge 2$ and $p\ge n$. Let $C$ denote the Cartan matrix of type $A_{n-1}$, with inverse $C^{-1}$. Let $\rho=(n-1,n-2,\dots,1,0)\in\mathbb Z^n$, and let $e_1=(1,0,\dots,0)\in\mathbb Z^n$. For a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ let $\ell(\sigma)$ denote its length, and write $\sigma\cdot v$ for the natural action of $S_n$ on $\mathbb Z^n$ by coordinate permutation.

For $L,M\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ and zero–sum vectors $k=(k_1,\dots,k_n),\ k'=(k'_1,\dots,k'_n)\in\mathbb Z^n$ with $\sum_i k_i=\sum_i k'_i=0$, define
$$T''(L,M,k,k')\ :=\ \prod_{i=1}^{n}\binom{M+L-k_i+k'_i}{L-k_i}_q,$$
where $\binom{a}{b}_q=\frac{(q)_a}{(q)_b(q)_{a-b}}$ when $0\le b\le a$ and zero otherwise, with $(q)_m=\prod_{j=1}^m(1-q^j)$.

For each $k\in\mathbb Z^n$ with $|k|:=\sum_i k_i=0$ and $\sigma\in S_n$, define an integer exponent $\phi_{p,k,\sigma}$ by
$$\phi_{p,k,\sigma}\ =\ \tfrac{p(p-1)}{2}\,k\cdot C\,k\ -\ k\cdot(p\rho-(p-1)\sigma\cdot\rho)\ +\ \ell(\sigma).$$

On the other side, let $\mu=(\mu^{(1)},\dots,\mu^{(n-1)})$ range over tuples of compositions (with the usual integrality/length restriction of the $A_{n-1}$ supernomial hierarchy: $\mu^{(b)}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}^{N}$ for a fixed large $N$, satisfying the standard congruence conditions making all subsequent $q$-binomials nonzero). Put
$$\eta\ :=\ nL\,(C^{-1}e_1\otimes e_1)\ -\ (C^{-1}\otimes C)\,\mu,$$
and define
$$\binom{\mu+\eta}{\mu}_q\ :=\ \prod_{b=1}^{n-1}\prod_{j\ge 1}\binom{\mu^{(b)}_j+\eta^{(b)}_j}{\mu^{(b)}_j}_q.$$

Conjecture (to be proved). For all $L,M\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ and all $p\ge n$,
$$\sum_{\substack{k\in\mathbb Z^n\\ |k|=0}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}(-1)^{\ell(\sigma)}q^{\phi_{p,k,\sigma}}\,T''\!\bigl(L,M,\,pk-\sigma\cdot\rho+\rho,\,(p-1)k-\sigma\cdot\rho+\rho\bigr)$$
$$=\ \sum_{\mu}q^{\,\tfrac12\,\mu\,(C^{-1}\otimes C)\,\mu}\ \binom{M+nL-\sum_{b=1}^{n-1}C^{-1}_{1,b}\mu^{(b)}_1}{nL}_q\ \binom{\mu+\eta}{\mu}_q.$$

Prove this identity. (The case $p=n+1$ is known from a Gessel–Krattenthaler-type cylindric-partition identity; establish the general case.)
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as a computer-checked open problem in the survey by Schilling and Warnaar on supernomial coefficients and Bailey's lemma. Subsequent work on the A_{n-1} Bailey lemma and on cylindric partitions (including the A_2 Rogers–Ramanujan revisited work and MacMahon-analysis approaches to cylindric partitions) has continued, but no source recovered in the search explicitly establishes this general p ≥ n identity beyond the known p = n+1 case. Its current status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers–Ramanujan-type Identities (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: States conjectural cylindric-partition-motivated identity supported by computer checks; p=n+1 case is the Gessel–Krattenthaler identity.
status_evidence.claim: Original statement is open and supported only by computer checks.

status_evidence.title: The A_2 Rogers–Ramanujan Identities Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Cylindric partitions used to rederive A_2 Rogers–Ramanujan identities.
status_evidence.claim: Related cylindric-partition identities have been treated in special low-rank cases but not the general conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A MacMahon analysis view of cylindric partitions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on cylindric partition generating functions.
status_evidence.claim: Active area; no direct resolution of the stated general identity located.
